findings.finding: Canonical-bridge single-vintage coverage collapse: for fields aggregated across the frozen 410-filer panel, the sector vintage locks to the MAX effective date across participating filers and includes only filers reporting at that exact date. Sectors containing one laggard fiscal-calendar filer sit at coverage 0.025-0.125, so the proposals' declared coverage gates (>= 0.60 a4_h1/a4_h2/a5_h1; >= 0.40 a6_h1) empty their cross-sections (declared series constructible at 0/30, 4/30, 0/30, 2/44 ticks respectively). The proposals' own 'never emptied by construction (>= 9 sectors)' claims (a4_h1.json:29, a4_h2.json:30) are falsified on the frozen store. Root cause: A3's P2 coverage census (p2_pit_data_audit_sec.json checks.A7_warmup_coverage) measures pre-S0 AVAILABILITY fractions (filers with any gated record), which the proposals quote as if they certified per-tick single-vintage coverage.
findings.owner_actions_scope: A1/A9-F adjudication; A7-N does not repair.

findings.finding: A5-H2 (Section 1.1 confirmatory front door) fails the preregistered A7-N shape gate: mean |rho| 0.319 > 0.20 vs the V4 semivariance-SHAPE anchor (max 0.655, 30/30 ticks, 10-11 sectors). The level-axis ancestry is documented as required (mean 0.919, max 1.000 vs the V4 vol-level control; rho 1.000 vs the 63-session variance level - the anchor is the level axis by monotone equivalence). Additionally 6/30 slots breach the preregistered stale-control rank-rho bound of 0.90 (max 0.955), while basket membership differs at 90% of slots (the L7 rank-identity failure mode is absent).

findings.consequence: Recorded against any future pairing of these families at selection.

Schedule prose discrepancies (recorded, not verdict-driving): a6_h2 claims 9 eligible sectors from S0 start with XLRE joining ~2019-06, but XLRE's snapshot history (from 2015-10-08) satisfies the >= 252-session rule from S0 start (measured 10 from start, 11 from the 2019-08-05 tick); a6_h1's early-set prose omits XLV from its own census (measured 8 sectors early, not 7); a4_h1's '>= 9 sectors eligible at every tick' and a4_h2's '>= 9 sectors eligible at every tick' claims are falsified (see A7N-F1/F2).

method.pnl_statement: NO PnL, NO portfolio returns, NO scored metrics were computed anywhere in this audit; feature/rank arithmetic only; every read S0-bounded (<= 2025-07-31).
method.series_policy: Declared constructions first (proposals' own gates on the canonical bridge). Where the declared series is degenerate on the frozen store, a clearly-labelled diagnostic/fallback series (one declared gate suspended, everything else identical) is measured so lineage evidence exists; non-constructibility of the declared series is itself recorded per tick and is terminal pre-selection evidence. A diagnostic series can never raise a verdict.
method.spearman: average ranks, Pearson on ranks; a pair is measured at a tick only over the common sector set (proposal-eligible intersect reference-ready) with >= 6 sectors
method.summary: Spearman rank correlation (average ranks, Pearson on ranks) of anchor feature vectors per proposal decision tick over the common sector set (proposal-eligible intersect reference-ready, minimum 6 sectors); V4 references reconstructed with the V4 terminal modules; SEC keys via the canonical bridge pit_conditioning.aggregate_sector_asof with each proposal's declared max_filing_gap_days and coverage floors; zero PnL.

overall_novelty_verdict.statement: Five of six blind proposals are INELIGIBLE on measured pre-selection evidence: four SEC-conditioned proposals cannot construct their declared anchor rank series through the canonical bridge on the frozen store (A7N-F1/F2), and the Section 1.1 confirmatory vol-level family fails its preregistered 0.20 shape-anchor gate (A7N-F3). Only SFV5-A6-H2 (cross-sector coupling state) is novelty-eligible: measurably distinct from every forbidden family and V4 anchor (worst mean |rho| 0.351) with its declared series fully constructible. No PnL was computed; this audit does not pre-judge A9-F feasibility or A1 selection for a6_h2.
